title: Long-prefix KV-cache TTL regression: synthetic eval + remediation plan
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: A recent configuration rollout that reduced KV cache TTL and switched kernel-selection for quantized runtimes coincided with a subtle quality regression observable only on long-prefix requests with unusual token boundaries. The degradation produced truncated or repetitive outputs for a small cohort of requests and escaped our nightly evals because those suites lacked representative long-prefix and tokenization-edge cases. This ticket records findings from the incident, immediate mitigations, and a concrete follow-up to add synthetic coverage and guardrails.
repro_steps: Replay anonymized production trace containing prefixes >8000 tokens and mixed UTF-8 control bytes
Observe generation: short repeated tokens, early termination, or attention window truncation in ~0.5-1% of traces
Compare trace logs showing eviction timestamps aligned with output anomalies
root_cause: Combined config interactions: (1) lowered KV cache TTL caused frequent evictions during long-prefix generation leading to incomplete KV state being used across continuation batches; (2) the new kernel-selection path for quantized attention kernels introduced an alignment sensitivity that shortened effective attention windows under rare token alignments. Individually each change passed existing checks; together they produced a failure mode not covered by our eval corpus.
mitigation_taken: Immediate rollback: restored KV_CACHE_TTL to last known stable value in canary regions (rolled back within 20 minutes)
Pinned kernel-selection to conservative quantized kernel for affected model variants
Added temporary log sampling for eviction events and attention window metrics to speed triage
observability_changes: New Grafana panels showing KV cache eviction rate by model, route, and prefix length
Trace enrichment: attach tokenization boundary histograms and eviction timestamps to sampled request traces
follow_up_tasks: ENG: Build synthetic eval harness that generates long-prefix sequences with varied tokenization edge cases and integrate into nightly regression (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2025-03-14)
ENG: Add server-side config guardrail preventing KV_CACHE_TTL < 60s for routes/models that enable prefix caching (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2025-03-08)
ENG: Implement integration tests exercising kernel-selection under extreme token alignment scenarios against quantized models (owner: Daniel Park, due: 2025-03-12)
SRE: Require canary synthetic eval pass (24h at 1% traffic) for any config change that touches cache or kernel-selection (owner: Noah Thompson, due: 2025-03-10)
DX: Publish incident runbook for silent-quality-regressions with immediate rollback commands and triage checklist (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2025-03-07)
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic long-prefix suite added to CI and included in nightly regressions
Config service blocks TTL values < 60s for prefix-caching-enabled models unless manually overridden with justification
At least two CI integration tests reproduce the previous failure mode and pass on runtime-1.20
Canary policy enforces 24h synthetic-eval stability at 1% traffic before global rollout
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/224 -- canary rollout policy for config changes
notes: Highest failure rate observed on routes mixing long system prompts with user code blocks; tokenization creates uncommon boundary tokens in these cases.
Preliminary impact: ~0.6% of canary requests showed short-output failure; 72% of those correlated with a cache eviction within the response window.
Recommendation: prioritize synthetic coverage and conservative guardrails over opaque optimizations that can mask regressions in telemetry.
Future synthetic samples should be seeded from anonymized production prefixes to increase realism of the eval set.
